title: Lunceford's sax section, Willie Smith and Jimmy Crawford's two-beat
summary: Willie Smith played so loudly that nothing was written for the reeds, and drummer Jimmy Crawford's two-beat style defined the band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, I was going to ask you about that. I mean, now, you've had a lot of experience with different bands. How did you feel about that sax section?
With Lunceford?
Yeah.

It was a novelty section, and the powerhouse was Willy Smith. And so that made it different from other bands, because he was so strong. He played saxophone so loud that we never did write any in the background, at no time, with the reeds.
You think he played too strong?

Oh, yeah, he was as loud as the whole brass section. And whenever the reeds was playing a little harmonies, Smith would be on his horn and we didn't write him no part because he could never get it down. He'd be strong.
Really, then he was too strong.
Yeah, yeah. They liked him too strong where he really played, so he just (unintelligible). That was one of the secrets of the band.
And then, Crawford had a lot to do with that band.
Yeah.
Because he had his own style on the drum. That two-beat thing and all that helped Lunceford's band. I imagine that would work all right now, I guess. Two beats, like that.
Well, the way they did it, it wasn't corny, was it?
Well, Sy is doing in now, I think.
Oh, yes.
That's what the boys say.
And people like it. Yeah, because the rhythm section, apart from Crawford, wasn't that strong, was it?
No, because Mose was a very -- he wasn't a real -- you would say, a great bass player.
No.
He was just a two-beat man.
Yeah.

So I guess that helped. Because if we'd got some other guy that was strong in another style, it would have confused the thing. So he just wrote on top of Crawford. Crawford was the leader. Crawford played first drums in the band, and Mose played second fiddle.
